newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA T-BILL MARKET DULL EVEN AFTER RATE CUT.
newsitem.headline: MANILA T-BILL MARKET DULL EVEN AFTER RATE CUT.

text.p: The secondary market of treasury bills saw little activity even after the central bank dropped its overnight borrowing rate to 14 percent from 18 percent, traders said.

A decline in interest rates usually spurs banks to position on bills ahead of a further slide in rates. But banks were wary because the central bank also raised liquidity reserves to five percent from four percent to contract liquidity and moderate the impact of lower rates on the peso.
"Nobody is buying. It's wait and see at the money market. They don't know if liquidity will tighten," one trader said.
"Banks are still cautious because of the instability in the peso-dollar market," another trader said.
However, some banks have started picking up short-term bills before the central bank brings down again its overnight rates.
In line with the cut in the central bank's rates, banks quoted lower bid and offer rates for T-bills.
A Reuters poll of seven financial institutions gave bids of 13.90/14.25 percent for the three-month bills.
